extract.note: Left out. (1) Every file that is not a subset's text (images, scripts, lock files, logs, statistics, the cards, the paper, the tests, the per-subset csv lists). (2) data/*/metadata.parquet: the dataset card says "Synthetic metadata is stored as data/{dataset}/metadata.parquet. These annotations were generated with ellamind/propella-1-4b", another company's model (docs/licenses.md, "No distillation"). (3) tv2r: its card header says "license: cc-by-sa-4.0" while its License Information section says "The owner of this content is TV2 Regionerne, Denmark. Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International", a contradiction left out as a doubt. Subsets whose card license is not on the allowed list: retsinformationdk and domsdatabasen ("license_name: Danish Copyright Law", the card quoting "§ 9. Love, administrative forskrifter, retsafgørelser og lignende offentlige aktstykker er ikke genstand for ophavsret.", not a license on the list); dannet ("DanNet 1.0 License"); gutenberg ("Gutenberg License"); ncc_maalfrid and ncc_parliament ("license_name: NLOD 2.0": NLOD-2.0 waits for the linking test and is not in licenses.py's ALLOWED). (4) Machine transcripts: mosel_voxpopuli, whose card says "The recordings come from VoxPopuli and were transcribed by the MOSEL project using Whisper large-v3." and "The transcripts were generated automatically and have not been manually corrected."; mosel_youtubecommons, whose card says "MOSEL produced the transcripts automatically as part of its YouTube-Commons collection."; ft (labeled CC-0), whose card says "All records have a transcript produced by commercial Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) followed by postediting by linguists employed by Folketinget", left out as a doubt until the maintainer decides whether a post-edited commercial ASR transcript counts as another company's model output.

For text from Wikimedia's wikis, the owners of the text state its license. Wikimedia's license page for its dumps, https://dumps.wikimedia.org/legal.html, says: "Text: Except as discussed below, all original textual content is licensed under the GNU Free Documentation License (GFDL) and the Creative Commons Attribution-Share-Alike 4.0 License. Some text may be available only under the Creative Commons license; see our Terms of Use for details." and "Where this information conflicts with specific information in the Wikimedia Foundation Terms of Use, or with other information contained inside the dumps themselves, this description should be ignored. Those terms are controlling."

The Wikimedia Foundation Terms of Use, which every contributor accepts when publishing, section 7, "Licensing of Content", https://foundation.wikimedia.org/wiki/Policy:Terms_of_Use, says: "Text to which you hold the copyright: When you submit text to which you hold the copyright, you agree to license it under: Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License ("CC BY-SA 4.0"), and GNU Free Documentation License ("GFDL") (unversioned, with no invariant sections, front-cover texts, or back-cover texts). Reusers may comply with either license or both." and "Modifications or additions to material that you reuse: When modifying or making additions to text that you have obtained from a Project Website, you agree to license the modified or added content under CC BY-SA 4.0 or later". On attribution, it says that contributors agree to be attributed "Through hyperlink (where possible) or URL to the article to which you contributed (since each article has a history page that lists all contributors, authors and editors)".

Text contributed under CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported moves to the later version through that license's section 4(b), https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/legalcode: "You may Distribute or Publicly Perform an Adaptation only under: (i) the terms of this License; (ii) a later version of this License with the same License Elements as this License; (iii) a Creative Commons jurisdiction license (either this or a later license version) that contains the same License Elements as this License (e.g., Attribution-ShareAlike 3.0 Unported) ("Applicable License")."
